bib.title: Faster R-CNN: Towards Real-Time Object Detection with Region Proposal Networks

legacy_report:
SOURCE: "Faster R-CNN: Towards Real-Time Object Detection with Region Proposal Networks", Shaoqing Ren, Kaiming He, Ross Girshick, Jian Sun. This file is arXiv:1506.01497v3 (6 Jan 2016), the extended journal-style version. A NIPS conference version came first ([10]). The PDF itself does not name a TPAMI venue.
File: /Users/ramsey-wise/workspace/learn-ai-engineering/ai-engineering/08-multimodal-engineering/sources/ren-2016-faster-r-cnn.pdf

COVERAGE: Read all 66,022 chars. The body runs to char 56,426 and references from 56,426 to the end, which I skimmed for origins. The only text I passed over was the detection-label clutter extracted from Figures 5 and 6 and the glyph codes in Figure 4.

CLAIMS
- claim: The RPN is a 3×3 conv layer followed by sibling 1×1 cls and reg layers, run over the last shared conv map. It uses k=9 anchors per position: 3 scales times 3 ratios.
  number: k = 9; areas 128², 256², 512²; ratios 1:1, 1:2, 2:1
  setup: ZF (5 shared conv layers) or VGG-16 (13); single scale with shorter side 600 px; stride 16. COCO adds a fourth scale, 64².
  quote: "By default we use 3 scales and 3 aspect ratios, yielding k = 9 anchors at each sliding position."
  where: p4
- claim: Shared features make proposals almost free, and the whole system runs at 5 fps on VGG-16 against 0.5 fps with Selective Search.
  number: 10 ms vs 1510 ms; 198 ms vs 1830 ms total; 5 / 17 fps
  setup: Table 5, K40 GPU. SS runs on CPU. 300 RPN proposals.
  quote: "VGG RPN + Fast R-CNN 141 10 47 198 5 fps" / "ZF RPN + Fast R-CNN 31 3 25 59 17 fps"; the intro gives SS as "2 seconds per image in a CPU implementation"
  where: p8 (Table 5), p1
- claim: With 300 proposals the RPN matches or beats SS at 2000, and the advantage grows on COCO, especially at stricter IoU.
  number: VOC07 69.9 vs 66.9 (VGG); 07+12 73.2; COCO test-dev 42.1/21.5 vs 39.3/19.3 (mAP@.5 / @[.5,.95])
  setup: VGG-16. Fast R-CNN is trained on 2000 RPN proposals and tested on 300. The COCO baseline is SS-2000 in their own implementation.
  quote: "Faster R-CNN has 42.1% mAP@0.5 and 21.5% mAP@[.5, .95] on the COCO test-dev set. This is 2.8% higher for mAP@0.5 and 2.2% higher"
  where: p8 (Table 3), p11 (Table 11)
- claim: Ablations (Table 2) show where the gain comes from. Sharing features helps. The cls scores make the top-ranked proposals good. The reg layer matters more than the anchors themselves. NMS does not hurt accuracy.
  number: shared 59.9 vs unshared 58.7. In the SS-trained ZF detector: 100 props 55.1, 300 props 56.8, 6000 with no NMS 55.2, no-cls at 100 props 44.6, no-reg 52.1.
  setup: VOC07 test, ZF, Fast R-CNN detector.
  quote: "Using separate networks reduces the result slightly to 58.7%"; "when the reg layer is removed at test-time (so the proposals become anchor boxes), the mAP drops to 52.1%"
  where: p7–8
- claim: More than one anchor matters, but 3 scales alone does as well as 3 scales times 3 ratios. The loss weight λ hardly matters.
  number: 1 anchor 65.8–66.7; 3 scales × 1 ratio 69.8; 3×3 69.9; λ 1–100 within about 1%
  setup: Table 8/9, VGG-16, VOC07 trainval → VOC07 test.
  quote: "If using just one anchor at each position, the mAP drops by a considerable margin of 3-4%."
  where: p9
- claim: The two-stage cascade beats a one-stage dense detector built in OverFeat style.
  number: 58.7 vs 53.9
  setup: Table 10. ZF, unshared. Dense "proposals" are 20000 windows at 3 scales and 3 ratios, with 5-scale features.
  quote: "the one-stage system has an mAP of 53.9%. This is lower than the two-stage system (58.7%) by 4.8%."
  where: p10

Two more numbers if the note needs them:
- COCO pretraining lifts VOC07 to 78.8: "The extra data from the COCO set increases the mAP by 5.6%" (p11).
- Moving from VGG-16 to ResNet-101 raises COCO val from "41.5%/21.2% (VGG-16) to 48.4%/27.2% (ResNet-101)" (p11).

LIMITS:
- Every experiment uses single-scale input and stride 16. The authors concede: "accuracy may be further improved with a smaller stride."
- Training uses the 4-step alternating scheme. Approximate joint training is mentioned as "close results" with 25–50% less training time, but no table backs it. Exact joint training (gradients through the box coordinates) is "beyond the scope of this paper."
- The 10 ms vs 2 s comparison is GPU against CPU, which the authors call "inequitable" (p1).
- The authors say recall-vs-IoU is only loosely tied to mAP.
- Anchor hyperparameters were "not carefully chosen".
- Nothing on small objects beyond adding the 64² anchor for COCO.
- No feature pyramids. 5 fps is "near real-time", not real time.
- No NMS ablation at the detector stage. NMS at IoU 0.7 is applied only to the proposals.
- The paper never mentions vision-language region features. It cites image captioning (DenseCap [16]) only as an adopter. The bottom-up attention link has to come from another source.
- Dated: VGG/ZF backbones, Caffe/MATLAB code.

BUILDS ON:
- R-CNN, Girshick et al., CVPR 2014: box parameterisation and fine-tuning.
- Fast R-CNN, Girshick, ICCV 2015: detector, multi-task loss, smooth L1, RoI pooling.
- SPPnet, He et al., ECCV 2014.
- FCN, Long et al., CVPR 2015.
- Selective Search, Uijlings et al., IJCV 2013.
- OverFeat, Sermanet et al., ICLR.
- MultiBox, Erhan et al., CVPR 2014 / Szegedy et al., arXiv 2015. Its 800 k-means anchors are not translation-invariant.
- VGG-16, Simonyan & Zisserman.
- ZF, Zeiler & Fergus.

CODE: No snippets. The useful formula is Eq. 2 on p5: "tx = (x−xa)/wa, t y = (y−ya)/ha, tw = log(w/wa), t h = log(h/ha)". The loss is Eq. 1 (p5), with Ncls=256, Nreg≈2400 and λ=10.

FIGURES: Figure 3 (p4) is the one to use. Caption: "Left: Region Proposal Network (RPN). Right: Example detections using RPN proposals on PASCAL VOC 2007 test." It shows the sliding window, the 256-d intermediate layer, the 2k scores and 4k coordinates, and the k anchor boxes in a single diagram, so anchors are understood at a glance. Figure 1 (p2), which compares image, filter and anchor pyramids, would be a second choice.

PROBLEMS: Without fontTools, pypdf printed warnings, but the text came out clean. The Figure 4 plot text is glyph codes and cannot be read. In Table 8, rows of the extraction run together ("65.82562 1:1 66.7" is 65.8 at 128² and 66.7 at 256²). Superscripts are flattened ("1282" means 128²). There were no embedded instructions.
